comments.author: asmeurer
comments.body: This isn't a strong oppose, but I don't necessarily feel we need a mixin class just for a single (short) method.

comments.author: eric-wieser
comments.body: This single short method (`_repr_latex_`) is monkey-patched by `init_printing`. By providing it in a base class, user classes can subclass this class to opt-in to the monkey-patching.

comments.author: asmeurer
comments.body: Those are my only comments here. I didn't realize we already had a DefaultPrinter class. It makes sense to just extend that class to support Jupyter, and to use it in the core. I would do it without changing the name or module name, so we don't break API if anyone was already using this. We should also double check the classes that currently use DefaultPrinting work correctly with this (looks like stuff in the polys and group theory).

comments.author: eric-wieser
comments.body:
See my comments above - the sorting out of `__str__` vs `_sympystr` is something I don't want to deal with in this patch, as it touches way too many things.

> I would do it without changing the name or module name, so we don't break API if anyone was already using this.

I've left behind an alias, so there's no API breakage here.

> We should also double check the classes that currently use DefaultPrinting work correctly with this.

The full list of those classes is:

* `sympy.combinatorics.fp_groups.FpGroup`
* `sympy.combinatorics.fp_groups.FpSubgroup`
* `sympy.combinatorics.free_groups.FreeGroup`
* `sympy.combinatorics.pc_groups.PolycyclicGroup`
* `sympy.combinatorics.pc_groups.Collector`
* `sympy.polys.agca.extensions.ExtensionElement`
* `sympy.polys.domains.pythonrational.PythonRational`
* `sympy.polys.fields.FracField`
* `sympy.polys.fields.FracElement`
* `sympy.polys.polys.PolyRing`
* `sympy.polys.polys.PolyElement`

You're right, it causes the default latex printer to be engaged for these types, which looks bad.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/425260/84518817-2b1dd200-acc9-11ea-8cc7-022e96b174d4.png)

Should I go back to having separate `StringPrintable` and `LatexPrintable` classes?

+"""
+Base class to provide str and repr hooks that `init_printing` can overwrite.
+
+This is exposed publicly in the `printing.defaults` module,
+but cannot be defined there without causing circular imports.
+"""
+from typing import Any
+
+
+class Printable:
+    """
+    The default implementation of printing for SymPy classes.
+
+    This implements a hack that allows us to print elements of built-in
+    Python containers in a readable way. Natively Python uses ``repr()``
+    even if ``str()`` was explicitly requested. Mix in this trait into
+    a class to get proper default printing.
+
+    This also adds support for LaTeX printing in jupyter notebooks.
+    """
+
+    # Note, we always use the default ordering (lex) in __str__ and __repr__,
+    # regardless of the global setting. See issue 5487.
+    def __str__(self):
+        from sympy.printing.str import sstr
+        return sstr(self, order=None)
+
+    __repr__ = __str__
+
+    # We don't define _repr_png_ here because it would add a large amount of
+    # data to any notebook containing SymPy expressions, without adding
+    # anything useful to the notebook. It can still enabled manually, e.g.,
+    # for the qtconsole, with init_printing().
+    def _repr_latex_(self):
+        """
+        IPython/Jupyter LaTeX printing
+
+        To change the behavior of this (e.g., pass in some settings to LaTeX),
+        use init_printing(). init_printing() will also enable LaTeX printing
+        for built in numeric types like ints and container types that contain
+        SymPy objects, like lists and dictionaries of expressions.
+        """
+        from sympy.printing.latex import latex
+        s = latex(self, mode='plain')
+        return "$\\displaystyle %s$" % s
+
+    _repr_latex_orig = _repr_latex_  # type: Any

review_comments.author: eric-wieser
review_comments.body:
```suggestion
Base class to provide str and repr hooks that `init_printing` can overwrite.

This is exposed publicly in the `printing.defaults` module,
but cannot be defined there without causing circular imports.
```

review_comments.author: asmeurer
review_comments.body:
> Natively Python uses ``repr()``
    even if ``str()`` was explicitly requested.

I don't understand what this sentence is saying. How does this change the behavior of Python calling repr when the user calls str? Is this referring to the behavior where Python uses `repr` on `str(list)`, or something else?

review_comments.author: asmeurer
review_comments.body: Perhaps this logic should be moved to the class (and we can probably do the same for png).

review_comments.author: asmeurer
review_comments.body: I think it should be doable with `__getattr__`, unless there's some technical detail about it I'm missing.

review_comments.author: asmeurer
review_comments.body: Maybe we should rename `__str__` above to `_sympystr`.

review_comments.author: asmeurer
review_comments.body: Oh I never realized this was here. Why not just put the new class in this file, instead of creating a new file?

review_comments.author: asmeurer
review_comments.body: Same here and with the other non-Basic classes. The mixin will define `__str__`, so we should probably rename `__str__` to `_sympystr`.

review_comments.author: asmeurer
review_comments.body: That's better too because we don't have an invalid flag on `__str__` this way.

review_comments.author: asmeurer
review_comments.body: This will also allow us to do the right thing by recursively calling `printer.doprint`.

review_comments.author: asmeurer
review_comments.body:
I guess this was from the old class. This is probably what was meant:

```py
>>> class Test:
...     def __repr__(self):
...         return 'repr'
...     def __str__(self):
...         return 'str'
>>> str([Test()])
'[repr]'
```

It's the reasoning why we keep `repr` and `str` the same for SymPy types.

review_comments.author: asmeurer
review_comments.body: Or better just add the methods to this class. No need to rename things.

review_comments.author: eric-wieser
review_comments.body:
We cant use this class in core/basic, as it creates circular imports - so we have no choice but to move it to a file somewhere in core..

I figured since no one really knew that this existed, it was a good opportunity to pick a more understandable name. I'm can change it back if you want me to, but I'd argue the new name is way clearer. Using gerunds as a class name is very odd.

review_comments.author: eric-wieser
review_comments.body: This is quite a can of worms, and something I'd prefer to handle in a follow up patch. There are whole subpackages using wierd patterns like this.

review_comments.author: eric-wieser
review_comments.body:
Hmm, this caused a regression in ipython plaintext printing of `MatrixBase`. The summary is:

* previously, we had an explicit pretty printer registered directly for `MatrixBase`, which was used after callling `init_printing`.
* now that we only register one for the base class, `MatrixBase.__repr__` is used instead of the pretty printer, as that's 
"more specialized".
